title: Giorgos Seferis's birth chart
metaDescription: Giorgos Seferis's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 22.4° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mars holds a square to Jupiter at 0.7° — close enough to weld drive to expansion. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 22.4° into Pisces — the third decan, which the old scheme hands to Mars. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 8.8° Aries; Venus stands at 3.1° Taurus; Mars stands at 9.8° Pisces. The tradition reads thought that arrives already in motion from Mercury, attraction that grows by reliability from Venus, effort that surges when it matters from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Mars and Jupiter — a square holding at 0.7°. A square is friction that produces motion — the aspect the tradition credits with building capability precisely by refusing to be comfortable. Behind it, Venus trine Saturn at 1.1°, and Mercury trine Jupiter at 1.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Pluto while both square Mars. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. Venus in Taurus at 3.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 10.5° is in domicile; Saturn in Capricorn at 4.2° is in domicile. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 fire, 2 water, 2 earth, 2 air by element and 6 mutable, 2 fixed, 2 cardinal by mode. All ten bodies ran direct that day — a chart with no apparent reversals anywhere in it.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Leo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.9° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 20.6°.
